Stripe dispute evidence: what does Stripe list for each reason?

Stripe's own evidence lists for fraudulent, product not received, product unacceptable, subscription canceled, duplicate, credit not processed and unrecognized disputes, with the Dashboard labels. Physical products, plus digital.

The stepsCopy a response outline

Free. Not affiliated with Shopify Inc. Not legal advice. Not sure what you have? Try the evidence picker. Want it written for you? $5

The short answer

  1. Stripe's documentation sorts every card or payment-method reason code into one of eight categories, and lists recommended evidence for each, separately for physical products, digital products or services, and offline services.
  2. Each piece of evidence goes under a named type in the Dashboard form or API, such as shipping_tracking_number or customer_communication. You can submit one file per evidence type, so combine files of the same type.
  3. Match the evidence to the reason. Stripe's own example: a clearly stated return policy is not relevant to a claim that the product never arrived.
  4. You get one opportunity to submit. Stripe forwards the response to the issuing bank and you cannot edit it or add files afterwards.
  5. Stripe says it does not influence the outcome, which is decided by the cardholder's bank.

Source: Stripe Documentation: Dispute reason code categories; Stripe Documentation: Respond to disputes; Stripe Documentation: Dispute evidence best practices, read 4 October 2026.

The steps

  1. Open the dispute in the Stripe Dashboard and read the category and any claim details the bank supplied.
  2. On the first page of the form, say why you believe the dispute is wrong and the product type of the purchase. Stripe uses that to recommend evidence.
  3. Pick your category below and gather the items for your product type.
  4. Upload one file per evidence type, summarise what each shows, and present things in the order they happened. Keep the combined file size within the 4.5 MB limit Stripe states.
  5. Tick the final-response box and submit.

The evidence checklist

Physical product lists, as Stripe publishes them on its Dispute reason code categories page. The label in each item is the Dashboard or API field. Digital products and services and offline services are summarised further down.

  • Credit not processed: your refund policy as provided to the customer [refund_policy]; how and where it was disclosed before purchase [refund_policy_disclosure]; why the customer is not entitled to a refund or further refund [refund_refusal_explanation]; customer communication [customer_communication]; arguments such as a refund already issued, whether the item came back, or a withdrawn dispute [uncategorized_text, uncategorized_file]
  • Duplicate: the charge ID of the apparent earlier duplicate [duplicate_charge_id]; an explanation of the difference [duplicate_charge_explanation]; documentation identifying the earlier payment, such as a separate receipt [duplicate_charge_documentation]; a shipping label or receipt for the disputed payment [shipping_documentation]; customer communication; itemised receipts showing separate purchases
  • Fraudulent and Unrecognized: link between the recipient and the cardholder, or that the cardholder has the goods [customer_communication, uncategorized_text, uncategorized_file]; signature and ID details if collected in person [customer_signature]; shipping address matching an AVS-verified billing address [shipping_address]; shipping documentation, date, carrier and tracking number [shipping_documentation, shipping_date, shipping_carrier, shipping_tracking_number]; other arguments, such as undisputed payments on the same card
  • Product not received: evidence the cardholder has the goods [uncategorized_text, uncategorized_file]; customer communication; signature [customer_signature]; shipping address, documentation, date, carrier and tracking number
  • Product unacceptable: the product as you represented it [product_description, uncategorized_file]; customer communication; your refund policy and how it was disclosed [refund_policy, refund_policy_disclosure]; arguments such as whether the item was returned, a replacement sent, a refund issued or the dispute withdrawn
  • Subscription canceled: how and when the cancellation policy was shown [cancellation_policy_disclosure]; why the subscription was not canceled or why this payment is valid [cancellation_rebuttal]; a renewal notice or the customer's acknowledgement of continued use [customer_communication]; other arguments
  • General: Stripe says to contact the customer to find out why they disputed the payment

Digital products, services and offline services, as Stripe lists them

  • Fraudulent, Unrecognized and Product not received: the customer's IP address at purchase [customer_purchase_ip], name [customer_name] and email [customer_email_address], and server or activity logs showing the customer accessed or downloaded the product [access_activity_log].
  • Product unacceptable: the product as represented, customer communication, activity logs, and your refund policy and its disclosure.
  • Subscription canceled: the cancellation policy as shown [cancellation_policy], its disclosure, your rebuttal, and a renewal notice or acknowledgement.
  • Credit not processed and Duplicate: policy language and disclosure, your explanation, and customer communication.
  • Offline services (advance purchases such as event tickets and reservations, where Stripe says a cancellation policy can be material): Fraudulent and Unrecognized ask for evidence linking the recipient to the cardholder, a signature from someone authorized or known by the cardholder, and documentation that the service was provided with its date [service_date, service_documentation]. Product not received asks for evidence the cardholder received the service, a signature if possible, and the same service documentation. Product unacceptable asks for the service as you advertised it, customer communication, and your refund policy and its disclosure. Subscription canceled adds the date the cardholder began receiving the service [service_date] and documentation that it was provided. Duplicate adds a copy of a service agreement or documentation for the disputed payment [service_documentation].

Stripe's best practices for how to present it

  • Present chronologically, group by type (receipts, communications, policies, logs), summarise what each item shows, and keep text and images readable.
  • Keep it relevant, factual, professional and concise. Stripe says too little evidence is a problem and so is overwhelming the reviewer.
  • Banks do not review external content: no audio or video, no requests to call or email, no links to click. Mastercard evidence is limited to a combined 19 pages.
  • Stripe says it publishes a likelihood-of-winning score for submitted responses. We do not quote its percentages.

Special cases Stripe describes

  • Fraudulent Visa 10.4 disputes: Stripe checks your history for Visa Compelling Evidence 3.0 eligibility and tells you in the Dashboard and the email. For payments that might be under the liability shift, Stripe provides most of the evidence, such as the 3D Secure result.
  • Stripe says Visa 10.5 disputes are extremely rare and accept no evidence.
  • Compliance disputes: contesting a Visa or Mastercard compliance dispute carries a 500 USD (or local equivalent) network fee in addition to the dispute fees, which Stripe refunds if you win.

A cover note to paste into Stripe's text fields (ours)

Plain text. Replace every [bracket] with a fact from your records and delete any line you cannot back with a file.

Order [order number], [amount and currency], dispute category: [category shown].

[One or two plain sentences on the key fact for this category, only if you can show it.]

Evidence, in the order events happened
1. [Date]: [what happened] ([evidence type label], [file name])
2. [Date]: [what happened] ([evidence type label], [file name])
3. [Date]: [customer communication, or: the customer did not contact us before the dispute]

[Name], [store name]

Never state anything you cannot prove. Every sentence in the response should point to a file you can attach. Delete any line you have no file for.

Common mistakes

  • Uploading several files for one evidence type. Stripe says combine them into one.
  • Sending policy evidence for a product-not-received claim. Stripe says it is not relevant there.
  • Adding links or 'call us' requests. Stripe says banks will not review external content.
  • Submitting before the file is complete. Stripe says there is one opportunity and you cannot amend it.
  • Using Shopify's reason names as if Stripe's were the same. Stripe maps each network or payment method code into its own eight categories, and the evidence types differ.

Questions merchants ask

Where does Stripe list evidence for each dispute reason?

On its Dispute reason code categories page, under category defense guidelines, with a selector for the category and for physical product, digital product or service, or offline service.

Is Stripe's category the same as the reason on my Shopify chargeback?

Not always. Stripe sorts each Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover, Klarna and PayPal code into one of eight categories. Shopify's reason names are similar but come from Shopify's own help pages. Use the category shown on your own dispute.

How many files can I upload per evidence type?

One. Stripe says to combine items of the same type into a single multi-page file, within a 4.5 MB combined limit.

What if the customer says they withdrew the dispute?

Stripe's withdrawal page says to submit evidence anyway: many issuers treat no evidence as accepting liability, and a withdrawn dispute still counts against your dispute rate.

What do I do if my category is General?

Stripe says General is an uncategorized dispute, rare for cards, and tells you to contact the customer to find out why they disputed the payment.

What we could not confirm

We read Stripe's physical product lists in full and the digital and offline service lists in summary. Fields and wording can change, so check the live page. How a Stripe dispute shows inside the Shopify admin was not confirmed. Rules and deadlines can change, so use the due date and form on your own dispute.
